record.paper_title: The origin and evolution of transition discs: successes, problems and open questions
record.original_question: Are the objects called pre-transition discs—discs that otherwise resemble transition discs but retain either a small amount of optically thin inner dust or a radially thin optically thick inner wall near the dust-destruction front—actually evolutionary precursors of transition discs, and is there any evolutionary path connecting them to transition discs that show only photospheric emission out to the mid-infrared?

evidence.quote: Espaillat et al. (2010) labelled these discs as "Pre-transition discs", such that the small amount of inner dust could represent the final stages of its disappearance.

To date there is no evidence that these discs are precursors to transition discs or that there is an evolutionary path that connects these discs to transition discs that show only photospheric emission out to the MIR.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the study of circumstellar discs around young stellar objects, a "transition disc" is defined (for the purposes of this problem) as a protoplanetary disc whose spectral energy distribution shows only stellar photospheric emission from the near-infrared through the mid-infrared, indicating the absence of warm dust in the inner regions, while exhibiting strong far-infrared excess from an outer dusty disc. A "pre-transition disc" is defined as a disc that otherwise resembles a transition disc (i.e., has a large dust-depleted gap and a substantial outer disc) but additionally retains either (a) a small amount of optically thin dust within the inner cavity, or (b) a radially thin optically thick inner wall located near the dust sublimation (dust-destruction) front, producing measurable near-infrared excess.

Question: Are pre-transition discs (as defined above) evolutionary precursors of transition discs? More precisely, does there exist a continuous evolutionary pathway by which a typical pre-transition disc loses its remaining inner optically thin dust and/or its narrow optically thick inner wall to become a transition disc whose spectral energy distribution shows only photospheric emission from the near-infrared out to the mid-infrared? Provide observational, theoretical, or model-based evidence either establishing or ruling out such an evolutionary connection.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether pre-transition discs evolve into transition discs remains an open question in the protoplanetary disc community. Subsequent observational and theoretical studies (e.g., works on inner-disc dust clearing, dust filtration at gap edges, and SED modeling of disc populations) have characterized pre-transition and transition discs in detail but have not established a definitive evolutionary link, with multiple formation channels (dead zones, dust traps, photoevaporation, planet-induced gaps) producing each class. No conclusive evidence directly connecting pre-transition discs as precursors to mid-infrared photospheric transition discs has been reported.

status_evidence.title: The origin and evolution of transition discs
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews state that to date there is no evidence connecting pre-transition discs evolutionarily to transition discs with photospheric MIR emission.
status_evidence.claim: The evolutionary connection between pre-transition and transition discs is not established.
